title: Memory handshake spill controller and multi-tier fallback layers
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a coordinated "memory handshake" controller that mediates between the continuous batching admission path, the KV cache manager, and GPU spill/quantization mechanisms to prevent OOMs and provide deterministic graceful degradation. The controller will provide: (1) an admission ticket protocol that preserves latency SLOs while allowing safe batch contraction under tight memory; (2) a KV preemption handshake to evict low-priority cache entries with explicit bounds and async restoration; (3) a progressive host-spill + micro-quantization path for high-pressure conditions; (4) a multi-tier fallback ladder that chooses lower-cost/lower-fidelity model variants automatically with retry/backoff semantics. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and a staged rollout for the controller and the fallback ladder on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Admission tickets reduce burst OOMs by >90% in the synthetic long-sequence workload used in perf-lab
KV preemption handshake evicts entries deterministically and restores 95% of evicted KV within 120s under normal load
Progressive host-spill path completes token generation with at most 3x latency degradation (95th percentile) compared to baseline, without causing GPU OOMs
Fallback ladder successfully routes 100% of overflow requests to an appropriate model variant and records an automatic A/B tag for quality regression analysis
End-to-end integration test covers admission rejection, KV eviction/restore, host-spill, micro-quant path, and fallback routing in CI
Monitoring dashboards show token-level cost, per-route fallback rate, and GPU memory watermark; automated alert fires when fallback rate >1% for 5m
implementation_notes: Core pieces: admission-ticket generator in request router; lightweight kv eviction API that tags evicted keys with ttl and priority; spill controller that first attempts device-to-host spill, then on-device micro-quant path; fallback ladder service that maintains model compatibility matrix and quality cost budgets. Controller exposes telemetry: ticket decisions, evict reasons, spill durations, fallback decisions and quality tags. Use existing kernel selection hooks to prefer quant-friendly kernels when micro-quant path selected.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Architecture review with runtime and kv teams. Agreed on ticket handshake message format and eviction TTL semantics. Action: Miguel to prototype eviction API.

2026-02-18: Prototype of admission tickets implemented. Initial experiments show 2x reduction in immediate OOM failures but increased tail latency for some batches — investigating batch contraction thresholds.
2026-02-24: KV eviction API merged; added async restore worker. Observed restore churn when memory flaps; added stabilization window to avoid thrash.

2026-03-01: Host-spill shim landed behind feature flag. Early lab tests show host-spill avoids OOM but at 4x latency degradation; tuning progressive spill chunk size reduced degradation to ~2.5x. Next: integrate micro-quant path to reduce host-spill cost.
2026-03-01: Began drafting rollout plan and dashboards. Need SRE approval for canary on Dedicated clusters.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive eviction can cause quality regressions due to missing KV prefixes. Mitigation: Tiered eviction based on request priority and implement soft-restore hints for high-value routes.
Risk: Host-spill increases CPU and memory pressure on nodes. Mitigation: limit concurrent spills per host and implement backpressure to router to shed low-priority requests early.
Risk: Automatic fallback may obscure regressions. Mitigation: tag every fallback with deterministic trace_id and route to evaluation pipeline to track drift and trigger rollback if quality drops.
Risk: Rollout could increase cost unpredictably. Mitigation: cost guardrails in rollout (percent budget, kill-switch alert) and telemetry to show per-token cost delta.
review_feedback: Leah Chen (PM): Request to add customer-facing SLO language and a graceful UX for API clients indicating degraded fidelity when fallback used.
Omar Patel (Principal Engineer): Proposed reducing host-spill chunking and prefer micro-quant when model supports per-layer quant thresholds. Also suggested integration test for eviction thrash.
Design (J. Morales): Suggested a concise API-level header that signals requested fidelity hint and allows clients to opt into best-effort degraded responses.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal perf-lab validation behind flags (2 weeks). Phase 2: controlled canary on 5 Dedicated hosts with 1% of traffic and full telemetry (1 week). Phase 3: expand to 20% with cost guardrails and customer opt-in for degraded responses (2 weeks). Emergency rollback via feature flag. Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window and compare fallback-induced regression metrics.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: Memory Handshake Overview, Per-route Fallback Rate, KV Eviction Heatmap, Host-Spill Latency Distribution. Alerts: Fallback rate >1% for 5m; Eviction restore failure rate >2% for 10m; Host CPU >85% during spills. Pager escalation only if fallback rate >5% for 10m or customer-impacting routes affected.
